commands.review_summary:
The PR adds agent-core tool-name alias resolution for selected Claude Code-style calls and adds regression tests around direct, case-insensitive, and deferred resolver behavior.

PR surface: Source +76, Tests +277. Total +353 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main exact-matches model-emitted tool names against registered tools and returns not-found when only the canonical OpenClaw name is registered. I did not run a live current-main reproduction in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Needs author or maintainer follow-up for the deferred catalog and lifecycle-event defects, plus contributor-provided real behavior proof; the proof gap prevents repair automation routing.

target.title: fix(agent-core): resolve tool-name mismatches for Claude Code alias calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents trained on Claude Code emit tool names such as `KnowledgeSearch`, `Glob`, and `Grep`. These names don't exist in a stock OpenClaw runtime, producing `Tool X not found` errors and causing the model to retry the same call until it gives up.

LCM corpus analysis on a private deployment (2026-03-15 – 2026-07-01):

| Tool name called | Failures |
|---|---|
| KnowledgeSearch | 2,586 |
| Glob | 1,234 |
| Grep | 159 |
| **Total covered by this PR** | **3,979 across ~1,400 conversations** |
| Agent (not covered — see below) | 429 |

Representative failure trace (redacted):
```
tool_call   toolCallId=[redacted]  toolName=Glob  arguments={"pattern":"[redacted]"}
tool_result toolCallId=[redacted]  toolName=Glob  isError=true
            content=[{"type":"text","text":"Tool Glob not found"}]
```
The model retried twice more with the same tool name, got the same error, and gave up.

## Fix

Add `resolveToolAlias()` before the deferred-tool resolver in `resolveToolCallTool()`:

1. **Case-insensitive exact match** — catches capitalisation drift (e.g. `READ` → `Read`).
2. **Normalised alias map** — strips non-alphanumeric characters, then tries ordered fallback names:
   - `KnowledgeSearch` → `memory_search`, `knowledge_search`, `wiki_search`, `search`
   - `Glob` → `find`
   - `Grep` → `grep`

The alias table is intentionally scoped to tools with **argument-compatible schemas** — a single query/pattern string. That's why `Agent`/`Task` are **not** in this PR: Claude Code emits `Agent(prompt="...")` but `sessions_spawn` takes `task`, and rewriting arguments belongs in the deployment's own tool catalog (where full schema context lives), not in a shared alias table. Deployments that want the Agent alias can bind it themselves with the correct arg translation — this PR gets 92% of the failure class right without coupling the resolver to any one tool's schema.

The deferred-tool resolver path is also alias-aware: when `resolveDeferredTool()` materialises a tool under its canonical name (e.g. `memory_search`) for an alias call (e.g. `KnowledgeSearch`), the dispatcher now accepts that as a valid resolution instead of throwing on the name mismatch — while still rejecting resolvers that return genuinely unrelated names.

When no alias matches, the not-found error now lists the agent's available tool names, which helps both the model self-correct and operators diagnose missing tool registrations.

The original tool-call name is preserved in the trajectory and tool-result audit identity so sessions are replay-identical to the pre-fix behaviour, except the call succeeds instead of erroring. Replay is deterministic because alias resolution is a pure function of the requested name and the agent's tool context.

## Tests

Six tests in the deferred-tool hydration suite (`agent-loop.test.ts`), 22/22 passing:

- `KnowledgeSearch` dispatches to `memory_search` (alias case).
- Case-insensitive lookup (`FIND` → `find`).
- Not-found error includes available tool list.
- `Agent` with a `sessions_spawn` tool present still returns not-found (regression against premature Agent alias).
- Deferred-tool resolver returning an alias-equivalent name (`memory_search` for `KnowledgeSearch`) is accepted and dispatched.
- Deferred-tool resolver returning an unrelated name (`not_related` for `KnowledgeSearch`) is still rejected.

Local: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts` → 22 passed.

## Evidence

**Before (pre-patch):** 3,979 `Tool * not found` failures across the three aliases covered by this PR (LCM analysis, full corpus 2026-03-15 – 2026-07-01) — see the table above. An additional 429 Agent failures are documented but intentionally out of scope for the reasons stated in the Fix section.

**After (post-patch):** the fix has been running as a local dist patch on a private OpenClaw deployment since 2026-07-02T14:43. Gateway restart at 2026-07-03T03:14 picked it up cleanly.

Post-restart grep of `gateway.log` (~500 lines of live fleet traffic since restart):
```
$ grep -c 'Tool \(KnowledgeSearch\|Glob\|Grep\) not found' gateway.log
0
```

Post-restart grep of agent-trajectory files (`~/.openclaw/agents/*/sessions/*.jsonl`) for `toolName` matching any of the three aliases with a ts >= 2026-07-03:
```
0 events
```

Note: the private fleet also applies a billing-proxy `promptAppend` mitigation that steers model calls toward native tool names, which is why organic alias-name calls no longer appear in the post-patch gateway log even before this fix's alias resolution kicks in. The resolver fix removes the need for the prompt-level workaround entirely and provides a correct fallback for deployments that don't apply such mitigations — the ones producing those 3,979 pre-patch failures. An auto-harvester (LaunchAgent, hourly) on the private fleet will attach a real dispatch trace to this PR the first time a model drifts and emits an alias call, but the mitigation currently suppresses that on our side.

## Redactions

Chat IDs, topic IDs, tool call IDs, agent identifiers, task content, session keys, file paths under the private deployment.
